title: Instrumentation tinker weekly (tracing & cost telemetry) — 2027-05-03
content:
Week summary (tl;dr):
- Focus: experiment to reduce trace ingestion costs without losing signal for regression detection.
- Tried a route-aware sampling config and a short-lived adaptive sampler prototype. Early results: ingestion cost down ~28% on staging; low-latency alerts still firing for the top-10 routes.
- Follow-ups: stabilize adaptive sampler, roll out a conservative config to prod for low-traffic routes, update dashboard heatmaps and billing anchors.

Monday — kickoff (Hannah lead)
- Quick sync 10:00am: scope and success metrics. Agreed success = 25% reduction in trace ingestion cost on staging + no missed P1 alerts for API surface.
- Action: Miguel to wire sampling flags into router (feature flag: obs.adaptive-sampler.v1).
- Notes to self: document how sampling decisions get stored in Redis vs local config.

Tuesday — prototype day
- Jordan pushed a micro-proxy that reads recent error rate + qps to decide sampling rate per route (PR 289).
- Ran 24h A/B on staging (50% baseline sampling, 50% adaptive): adaptive kept 98th percentile latency traces for high-error routes, reduced low-value traces for background batch jobs.
- Weirdness: one internal infra route saw sampling drop to 2% causing a gap in a regression test. Put guard rule: routes tagged "internal-critical" -> min sampling 15%.

Wednesday — dashboard and billing checkpoints
- Priya updated the trace ingestion dashboard (new tiles): daily spans ingested, cost/time delta, median spans per trace. Link: confluence note in linked_artifacts.
- Billing spike investigation: discovered delayed span compression job (OBS-UTIL-71) caused backlog that inflated daily costs on 2027-04-29. Fixed by bumping concurrency and adding a slow-job alert.
- Decision: enable compression job healthcheck in the rollout policy.

Thursday — incident rehearse + SLO check
- Mini postmortem drill for a synthetic latency spike. Verified tracing sampling still captured the root-cause trace when sampling floor = 10%. Good signal preserved.
- SLOs: telemetry ingestion SLO holds; we need an SLO for trace availability in evaluation pipelines (Priya to draft).

Friday — rollout plan + retro
- Rollout: a conservative rollout to prod for non-critical routes starting next week. Staged by traffic quantiles (0-20% low, 20-60% medium, 60-100% high).
- Retro notes: prototype worked but needs hardened observability for the sampler itself (metrics about sampling decisions, a sampling-explain API).
- Owner assignments: Miguel (sampler stabilisation), Jordan (feature flags + infra), Priya (dashboards + SLO doc), Ravi (billing anchors + compression health).

Technical dive: adaptive-sampler design (short explainer)
- Principle: keep trace signal for routes with high error/latency volatility, downsample predictable/background routes. Decisions are based on a rolling window (5m) of: error-rate, 95th latency change, and qps.
- Decision store: ephemeral in-memory for speed + periodic checkpoint to Redis for debugging.
- Safety nets: per-route min-sampling floor, tag-based overrides (internal-critical, customer-facing), and a time-decay boost if an alert fires.

Metrics / early numbers (staging A/B, 48h window)
- Spans ingested: baseline 2.1M/day -> adaptive 1.5M/day (-28%).
- Tracing cost (raw ingest + storage): baseline $4.6k/day -> adaptive $3.3k/day (-28%).
- Alert fidelity: P1 alert captures for top-10 routes preserved (100% in test).
- Missed low-priority traces increased but matched expectations.

Open questions / risks
- How to attribute cost savings to customer billing lines? (Ravi to map span tags -> billing anchors).
- Will adaptive decisions interact badly with profiling agents (which rely on 100% sampling)? Need an integration plan.
- Edge case: bursty jobs that are short-lived may be under-sampled and we could miss a regression. Mitigation: introduce burst-detection boost.

Action items (short list)
- Miguel: harden sampler config, add metrics (sampler_decisions_total, sampler_overrides_total). Due 2027-05-10.
- Priya: SLO draft for trace availability and update dashboards with cost anchors. Due 2027-05-07.
- Jordan: roll out feature flags to prod with safe gates + rollback playbook. Due 2027-05-11.
- Ravi: map span tags to billing anchors and validate cost allocation for Q2 forecast. Due 2027-05-14.
- Hannah: write a short runbook for the sampler and post to Confluence. Due 2027-05-06.

Meeting notes (raw snippets from standups)
- "Samplers need a way to explain why they dropped a trace — debugging costs us too much time." — Priya
- "If compression backlog recurs, throttle non-critical ingestion until cleared." — Ravi
- "Add a lightweight /sampler/debug endpoint that returns recent decisions for a route." — Jordan

References & artifacts
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/289
- Slack thread: #obs-sampling (see pinned message ts=1689984000)
- Jira: OBS-4123 (adaptive-sampler), OBS-UTIL-71 (compression backlog)

Notes to future self
- Keep experiment window >= 48h for diurnal effects.
- Save full trace captures for 1% of traffic for 7 days for retrospective debugging.
- Prepare a short customer-facing blurb: "We reduced internal trace ingestion to lower platform costs; your latency monitoring will not be affected."

Unresolved / parking lot
- Formal QA checklist for sampler changes (who signs off? QA? SRE?).
- Cost allocation automation for trace-level billing.

End of week mood: optimistic but cautious — cost wins are real, but we must not trade away debuggability for short-term savings.
